 --> New cyclone brewing over Bay of Bengal, likely to turn severe by November 17: IMD
 A depression over the Bay of Bengal is expected to intensify into a cyclonic storm on November 16 and a severe cyclonic storm on November 17, the IMD said. 
 Moneycontrol News 
 November 15, 2026 / 12:24 IST Share --> 
 --> 
 --> 
 --> 
 IMD forecasts a severe cyclonic storm over the Bay of Bengal by November 17. Check the latest cyclone alert, rainfall forecast and weather warnings. IMD forecasts a cyclonic storm over the Bay of Bengal.
 Depression to intensify into a severe storm by Nov 17.
 Karnataka previously aided Andhra Pradesh after Cyclone Arnab.

 The India Meteorological Department (IMD) on Sunday, November 15, said a depression over the Bay of Bengal is likely to develop into a cyclonic storm on November 16 before intensifying into a severe cyclonic storm on November 17. 
 According to news agency ANI, the weather system, which originated as a well-marked low-pressure area over the southeast Bay of Bengal, moved north-northwestwards and intensified into a depression at 5.30 am on Sunday. 
 The IMD said the depression was centred over the southeast and adjoining southwest Bay of Bengal, near latitude 9.0°N and longitude 86.9°E. 
 It was located approximately 700 km west-southwest of Sri Vijaya Puram (Port Blair), 860 km east-southeast of Chennai, 1,040 km south-southeast of Visakhapatnam and 1,160 km south-southeast of Gopalpur in Odisha. 
 What has the IMD forecast? 
 The weather department expects the system to continue moving north-northwestwards and strengthen into a cyclonic storm over the central parts of the south and adjoining west-central Bay of Bengal on November 16. 
 It is forecast to intensify further into a severe cyclonic storm over the west-central Bay of Bengal on November 17. 
 According to the IMD's November 15 tropical weather outlook, sustained winds could reach 90-100 kmph, gusting to 110 kmph, by the evening of November 17. The department has also projected further intensification over the following two days. 
 However, the IMD said weather models continued to differ on the system's subsequent movement, intensity and landfall location. 
 Rainfall forecast and warnings 
 The weather department has warned of deteriorating sea conditions across parts of the Bay of Bengal as the system strengthens. 
 In its earlier advisory, the IMD forecast heavy rainfall over the Andaman and Nicobar Islands until November 16, with isolated heavy rainfall likely over coastal Andhra Pradesh and Odisha on November 18 and 19. 
 Fishermen were advised to return to the coast by November 15 and avoid venturing into affected parts of the Bay of Bengal and Andaman Sea. 
 Region recovering from Cyclones Arnab and Murasu 
 The latest development comes weeks after Cyclones Arnab and Murasu struck India's eastern coast, damaging infrastructure in parts of Andhra Pradesh. 
 On November 2, Karnataka Chief Minister D K Shivakumar announced assistance to Andhra Pradesh following damage to electricity infrastructure caused by Cyclone Arnab. 
 According to an official release cited by ANI, Karnataka deployed 500 skilled powermen, 15 Palfinger trucks equipped with cranes and earth augers, and 25 tractor-based drilling machines to support restoration work. 
 Shivakumar also spoke to Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister N Chandrababu Naidu and assured him of the state's support. 
 The personnel were organised into teams of 10, supervised by junior or assistant engineers, with executive engineers coordinating restoration operations. 
 The IMD continues to monitor the developing system, with its track and eventual landfall location yet to be determined.
